newsitem.title: USA: Dow drifts lower by midday, Nasdaq stagnant.
newsitem.headline: Dow drifts lower by midday, Nasdaq stagnant.

text.p: Wall Street shares drifted lower in midday trading Thursday, relinquishing small morning gains to profit-takers but lacking the firm conviction needed to make a decisive move either up or down.
The Dow industrials were off 32 points, or 0.43 percent, at 7326, backing away from a session high of 7369 after opening lower.
The Nasdaq composite index was also soft, down 0.56 point at 1410. The long bond, which was seen providing some support to stocks, was up 9/32 to yield 7.01 percent.
"Trading is a bit on the sloppy side," said Greg Nie, a senior vice president of technical research at Everen Securities.

A combination of negative earnings announcements and share rating downgrades contributed to the market's uncertain sentiment, said John Gardner, chief equity strategist for Van Lieu Capital. "We are seeing a lot of fine-tuning going on," he said.
Dow component International Business Machines Corp was off 1-3/8 at 88-1/2. Salomon Brothers said it downgraded the stock to buy from strong buy because it hit a price target.
Among shares punished for disappointing earnings was Nike Inc, off 8-5/8 to 55.

The sneaker-maker said fourth quarter results would fall below expectations, forecasting earnings of $0.51 to $0.56 per share, compared to a First Call consensus estimate of $0.69. Nike cited a revenue shortfall.

Computer software publisher Novell Inc posted an unexpected earnings loss in the second quarter of $0.04 per share, compared to a loss of $0.15 a year earlier. It also said it planned to cut its workforce.
Novell shares were off 5/16 at 7-3/4.
"The market does not have a high degree of conviction," Gardner said. "It boils down to the fact that you now have to be very selective when buying individual names. It's a stock picker's market."
Joseph Battipaglio, chief investment officer at Gruntal, said the stock market has been strong in recent weeks and is due for a pull-back.
"On a very short-term basis, it's profit-taking," he said.
The stock market took some support from the bond market, as the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond slowly recovered to a seven percent yield.
"Stocks are holding in there, but they have missed many opportunities on the upside as bonds have come back toward a seven percent yield," Nie said.
Bond yields rose above seven percent this week on concerns about rising inflation and possible interest rate increases.
Stocks could remain in limbo until it is clear what the Federal Reserve will do to interest rates at its July meeting, Gardner said.
For stocks to rally again, the market needs to display higher volume and decidedly positive breadth, Nie said.
On the New York stock exchange, advancing issues outpaced declining issues by six to five. On Nasdaq, advancers narrowly outnumbered decliners.
Small capitalization and technology stocks continued to fare slightly better than the broader market, analysts said.
Among active issues, Boston Chicken Inc was off 1-1/8 to 17. The company said it was not satisfied with sales momentum in its Boston Market stores.
Time Warner Inc was down 1-1/2 at 47 after news that Seagram Co Ltd had sold more than half of its stake in the company for $1.39 billion.
((--Wall Street Desk 212-859-1730))
